entry.title: Show HN: Nuking the crap Claude left in the codebase - CCN (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: CCN Strips comments out of codebases, and comments ONLY, this isn't a regex parse that could potentially eat your code, no this actually makes a list and checks it twice. I, as a real developer, often leave bytes of comments in my own codebases then forget about them, AI models leave MEGABYTES and has NO memory, sometimes literally using comments as a FORM OF IT. Use this tool to clean your codebases of literal trash, or use it to review, very useful, end to end tested and verified against 2,700 iterations (not that you care or anything, it works, even on debian trixie with xfce desktop, and that's what matters, not the thousands of tests I ripped from the codebase before publishing it that end users dgaf about) As Stallman infamously says... Happy hacking ;) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49141107 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Sick of waiting for agents to run and then having to debug (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: I am an engineer and i spend so much of my time vibe coding using claude and its been great because I am able to get a lot done but its also incredibly frustrating. I spend so much time waiting for the agents to complete running, during which time i end up moving to another task. The context switching is so tedious. For more complex tasks, I would like for it to happen without my input. I try to give it multiple steps of instructions and let it to run and it works to an extent but it doesnt work when i have to periodically test things on a separate environment (like on a pre production environment with multiple settings). I would like for it to run its own tests, look at the logs and verify that its working and then get to the next step or retry. Kind of like a feedback loop that keeps getting monitored at all hours of the day. Are others running into this issue? And have you found any solution? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49141048 Points: 1 # Comments: 1
